core_obligations: Apply the degreewise result (proof lines 7802-7812): writing the colimit complex, the companion theorem gives the interchange of filtered colimits with the cohomology of each term of the complex.

Compare the two spectral sequences (proof lines 7813-7824): the cohomology of a complex is computed by the spectral sequence with first page given by the cohomology of its terms, and the bounded below hypothesis makes only finitely many terms contribute in each degree, independently of the index, so the two first pages are related by the colimit maps computed above.
Conclude (proof lines 7824-7827): the comparison of the first pages gives the comparison of the abutments, which is the statement.
proof_roadmap: Write both sides as abutments of the spectral sequence of a complex.
Use the bounded below hypothesis to make the first page comparison finite in each degree.
Apply the degreewise colimit theorem to identify the first pages and hence the abutments.
difficulty_reason: The lemma extends the degreewise compatibility of etale cohomology with filtered colimits to complexes of abelian sheaves on a directed limit of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes with affine transition morphisms (statement lines 7782-7799). The proof is a spectral sequence comparison: the degreewise theorem is applied to each term of the complexes (proof lines 7802-7812), the spectral sequences of a complex under the global sections functor are displayed, and the bounded below condition is used to show that only finitely many, index-independent terms contribute in each degree, giving the identification of the first pages and hence of the abutments (proof lines 7813-7827). The non-formal content is the finiteness bookkeeping that makes the comparison legitimate. The claim is H2: a spectral sequence comparison with the finiteness input used explicitly.
